title: Net Energy Metering and Net Billing

verified.claim: Solar customers on the older net-metering tariff keep it for 20 years from interconnection.
verified.quote: Pursuant to D.14-03-041, customer-generators are allowed to remain on the NEM 2.0 tariff for 20 years from the date they interconnected, or they are permitted to switch to the current tariff.

verified.claim: Systems connected since April 15, 2023 are on the net billing tariff, with a nine-year guarantee for the original customer only.
verified.quote: Nine-year legacy period: The original customer who causes a generation facility to be interconnected to the grid under the NBT is guaranteed the use of the NBT tariff for nine years.

title: CPUC Response to Executive Order N-5-24 (February 18, 2025)

verified.claim: Today the 20-year legacy period belongs to the solar system, not the customer; the CPUC has listed ending it when a home changes ownership as an option.
verified.quote: Tying legacy periods to the customer, not the system: currently, the 20-year legacy period before which NEM 1 and 2 customers are defaulted onto the NBT is linked to the installed system, not the customer. Systems could be converted to the NBT when the home changes ownership or at the end of the legacy period

verified.claim: Rent on an empty rent-controlled unit can be set freely for a new tenant.

agency: City and County of San Francisco, Treasurer & Tax Collector
title: Empty Homes Tax (EHT)

verified.claim: The San Francisco Empty Homes Tax (vacant units in buildings of three or more units) is not being collected: the Court of Appeal affirmed on September 11, 2026 that state law preempts it.
verified.quote: On September 11, 2026, the California Court of Appeal affirmed the trial court ruling, holding that the Empty Homes Tax is preempted by state law (Case Number: A172067). Pursuant to the court judgment and order, the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector will stop all work to collect the Empty Homes Tax. Property owners impacted by the tax will not be required to file or pay unless and until the appeals court's decision is reversed.
